RESEARCH VERDICT
Structured conviction overlay for the quantitative screen (does not replace the screen signal).
Verdict: caution
Risk: high
Confidence: 0.68
Rationale: Research weakens the buy: dividend screens pass but FY25 statutory FCF is negative and company FCF is below the $2.1bn dividend; HY26 FCF $352m vs $1,084m interim; CMD shifts payout to 20–40% of adjusted OCF.
RiskTags: cyclical, leverage, regulatory

The current `screening_snapshot.json` is a buy with Yahoo FCF of −$782m and TTM cash flow suppressed (empty quarterly cash flow). It has no `adjusted_signal`. July 2026 snapshots had `adjusted_signal` still at buy, with dividend-family passes (High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth), yield 5.6%, and PEGY 0.03. Those overlay tensions remain open: filing OCF of $7,192m matches the screen, but statutory OCF−CapEx FCF is negative (Yahoo CapEx $7,974m; filing investing cash flow $7.9bn), while company-adjusted FY25 FCF of $1,889m is still below the $2.1bn full-year dividend. HY26 company FCF of $352m does not cover the $1,084m interim. FY25 NPAT and diluted EPS fell 24% versus 2024, at odds with the GARP/Dividend Growth passes; the HY26 interim rose to 57 US cps from 53, so no interim cut is flagged. Gearing was 20.6% at 30 June 2026, outside the 10–20% target. The 5 November 2026 Capital Markets Day replaced the 80% NPAT payout with 20–40% of adjusted operating cash flow.

EVIDENCE
- [filings/bodies/9340a1fdbab35770.txt] "Record production offset lower realised prices resulting in net profit after tax (NPAT) of $2,718 million (24% lower from 2024) and underlying NPAT of $2,649 million (8% lower from 2024)." — FY25 earnings declined versus 2024; screen GARP/PEGY is not filing-aligned.
- [filings/bodies/9340a1fdbab35770.txt] "Operating cashflow $ million 7,192 5,847 23% Free cash flow4,5 $ million 1,889 (293) 745%" — Filing OCF matches the screen; company-adjusted FCF is positive, unlike Yahoo statutory FCF of −$782m.
- [filings/bodies/9340a1fdbab35770.txt] "which brings the full-year fully franked dividend to US 112 cps and maintains payout ratio at the top of the range at 80%. The value of the full-year dividend is $2.1 billion." — Dividend-family screens pass while FY25 DPS is 8% below 2024’s 122 cps and exceeds company FCF.
- [filings/bodies/9fbf9aecbbc93b03.txt] "Delivered operating cash flow of $3,013 million and free cash flow of $352 million." — HY26 company FCF; statutory investing outflow was $4,286m so OCF−investing is negative before NCI credits.
- [filings/bodies/9fbf9aecbbc93b03.txt] "The total amount of the interim dividend payment is $1,084 million which represents 80% of underlying NPAT for the first half of 2026." — HY26 dividend cover on company FCF is below 1.0×; no interim cut (57 vs 53 US cps).
- [filings/bodies/9fbf9aecbbc93b03.txt] "Gearing of 20.6%, marginally outside the target range of 10 - 20%, impacted by $655 million of new lease liabilities, a $419 million net cash outflow from hedge settlements" — Investment-cycle leverage and hedge cash outflows.
- [filings/bodies/68392f65b7829f4c.txt] "As at 30 September 2026, Woodside had liquidity of approximately $7,800 million and net debt (including lease liabilities) of approximately $8,900 million." — Liquidity down from $9.3bn at FY25; net debt still elevated into Q3.
- [filings/bodies/fa04f81d985fc89e.txt] "We announced a new distribution policy of 20 – 40% of adjusted operating cash flows.  We will prioritise 20% of adjusted operating cash flow as a base dividend" — Policy shift that can lower cash returns versus the 80% NPAT payout the screen used.

THESIS BREAKS
- Scarborough first LNG cargo slips beyond 2026, or a material cost/schedule break is disclosed on Trion or Louisiana LNG (first LNG targeted 2029; Woodside net capex $9.9bn).
- A subsequent dividend is set at the 20% of adjusted operating cash flow floor at a level below the HY26 57 US cps interim, or an interim cut is announced.
- Gearing moves further above the 10–20% band with a downgrade from the stated Moody’s Baa1 / S&P BBB+ ratings.
- Partner contributions on Louisiana LNG cease or reverse, so company-adjusted FCF remains negative while the $4.0–4.5bn 2026 capex guidance is spent.
